This use of the Bayesian framework reflects the scientific “learning cycle,” where prior or initial estimates are updated when new data become available. In this paper we outline a framework for statistical design of expert elicitation processes for quantifying such expert knowledge, in a form suitable for input as prior information into Bayesian models. results.title: Use of Expert Prior Elicitation for Clinical Research
results.content: Use of Expert Prior Elicitation for Clinical Research | Pharmaceutical Outsourcing - The Journal of Pharmaceutical & Biopharmaceutical Contract Services. * Use of Expert Prior Elicitation for Clinical Research. Use of Expert Prior Elicitation for Clinical Research. Expert prior elicitation follows an interview process in which experts are asked a series of questions regarding their beliefs about, for example, a treatment effect. Comparatively, informative priors can be created through historic data, expert elicitation or a blended method of the two, taking the belief or previous information available to give an idea of the expected treatment effect, safety profile or other measurements. Elicitation is the act of creating priors from data or opinions from experts. Often it is more feasible to use expert elicitation, for example, when there is limited or contrasting historic information available, experts can be used to establish a view, whilst the direct mathematical model may lead to a mixed and confused result. Experts are provided with a complete review of available information before being asked questions relating to the measurement of interest, which is collated into their individual elicitation (a distribution of their belief). Behavioral aggregation allows the individual elicitations to be combined with other experts and discussed as a group by the experts. Ensuring the patient population of interest and what measurement system is used allows comparability between the elicited prior and the trial. The aim is to elicit a single aggregate prior which represents the collective belief of experts based on the discussion of their individual priors, with as many rounds of elicitation and group discussion as needed. Specific elicitation software can be used to ensure that the information gathered from experts can be clearly visualized, allowing for easier interpretation and analysis by the experts both at an individual and a combined level. #### **Examples of Expert Elicited Priors for Rare Disease/Small Population Trials**. By producing a prior and having the trial run within a Bayesian framework, the plausible 150 patients would have enough information to produce an acceptable posterior distribution for realistic conclusions to be drawn. Expert prior elicitation is a valuable addition to clinical trial decision making.

results.title: How CFA Uses the Expert Elicitation Process to Inform Our Work | CFA: Qualitative Assessments | CDC
results.content: # How CFA Uses the Expert Elicitation Process to Inform Our Work. Expert elicitation is a structured process that involves convening subject-matter experts in disease topics and cross-cutting disciplines—to discuss questions that we have insufficient data to answer or solicit input on the likelihood of various outcomes or scenarios. The expert elicitation process then officially begins with recruiting relevant subject-matter experts and sharing relevant data and other project-related information with them. In many cases, expert elicitation processes involve experts assigning uncertainty levelsA to their answers to specific questions, as a way to provide an estimate of individual uncertainty. This uncertainty differs from our overarching confidence levels in our risk and scenario assessments, which incorporate the entire body of evidence, including expert judgment. The estimate is the number the expert comes up with when asked directly, but the expert would not be surprised if they updated their estimate significantly after more time to think and after receiving more information.
